title: Breaking the power wall in programmable photonics
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01960-w

A non-volatile photonic gate array based on ferroelectric domain switching eliminates static power consumption, pointing towards scalable and energy-efficient photonic integrated circuits.

title: Valleytronics on a single chip
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01975-3

The integration of light-programmable valley optoelectronic nanocircuits based on two-dimensional semiconductors has been limited by complex optical readout using bulk optics. Now, a chip integrates a metasurface with a waveguide and on-chip photodetectors to generate, sort, and read out optical valley signals in the near field, all at room temperature.

title: The path ahead for organic photovoltaics
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01963-7

Nature Photonics spoke with Yongsheng Chen from Nankai University, who was recently elected an Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, about milestones in organic photovoltaic research, key outstanding challenges and the breakthroughs needed to further develop the technology.

title: Silencing pain with infrared light
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01970-8

Lanthanide upconversion nanoparticles convert near-infrared illumination into local visible emission, enabling wireless optogenetic modulation of deep pain pathways.

title: A hot-electron-based plasmonic artificial leaf
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01969-1

Non-radiative plasmonic decay generates energetic charge carriers that rapidly thermalize; however, if captured quickly, these hot electrons can be harnessed for a range of applications. Now, a hot-carrier artificial leaf, made by gold-titanium dioxide plasmonic interfaces, demonstrates excellent performance for both in vivo bioelectronics and pixel-free artificial vision systems.

title: Attosecond leap in scanning tunnelling microscopy
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01971-7

Detection of attosecond transient currents at a sub-nanometre-sized gap between a probe tip and a sample is realized using tailored, two-colour, single-cycle light pulses.

title: Extensible universal photonic quantum computing with nonlinearity
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01962-8

An extensible photonic quantum computing architecture based on a fully programmable, scalable linear-optical network has been realized, and is enhanced by two addressable modules: an inline squeezing module for injecting nonlinear resources as input states and a Kerr interaction module for implementing effective nonlinear operations.
